title: An Israeli professor lost a prestigious US job offer after speaking out on Gaza. Now the university is paying him $250,000
excerpt: The University of Minnesota withdrew an offer for Raz Segal to lead its Center for Holocaust and Genocide Studies after an organized campaign against his hiring
content_html:
When the University of Minnesota (UMN) extended an offer to historian Raz Segal to lead its Center for Holocaust and Genocide Studies in June 2024, it did so upon the near-unanimous recommendation of a committee of academics after a rigorous search process. The scholars had enthusiastically praised Segal, with one committee member describing a presentation he gave as “breathtaking”.

But five days after making the offer, the university abruptly withdrew it, citing “perspective” it had received from members of the community. The reversal followed backlash over Segal’s criticism of Israel’s actions in Gaza, which he called “a textbook case of genocide” in an October 2023 op-ed published in Jewish Currents. Segal’s critics condemned the piece, published just days after the 7 October attacks in Israel, accusing him of justifying Hamas crimes – an assertion that Segal rejected and the article does not sustain.

Last week, more than two years since the offer was rescinded, Segal reached a $250,000 settlement with the university. As is standard with such settlements, the terms of the deal stipulate the payout is not an admission of wrongdoing on UMN’s part. The university did not respond to a request for comment.

Segal said the significant sum should encourage the dozens of scholars who have been punished for criticizing Israel with firings, suspensions and investigations to “fight back”.

The settlement came after Segal obtained dozens of emails through a public records request, revealing a pressure campaign on university officials by donors, legislators and pro-Israel activists. The documents shared exclusively with the Guardian, reveal how the university shifted from defending Segal to eventually walking back their decision to hire him.

“We cannot allow someone like Raz Segal a blatant anti Zionist to head the department of Holocaust studies [sic],” one donor wrote to the chair of the university’s board. “There are many who will pull there [sic] pledges to the university if this isn’t addressed.” According to Segal, hundreds of emails were sent to the university following the same template, indicating a coordinated campaign.

The Center for Constitutional Rights, which represented him, argued that the public university’s actions against Segal were unconstitutional, because they retaliated against him over constitutionally protected speech.

“Dr Segal had the courage to sound the alarm to try to prevent Israel’s genocide of Palestinians,” said Maria LaHood, the center’s deputy legal director. “And for this, the University of Minnesota administration overruled the will of its faculty and revoked his job offer in violation of the first amendment and fundamental principles of academic freedom.”

Segal, who is Jewish and a dual Israeli-US citizen, the grandchild of four Holocaust survivors and a scholar of the Jewish world and the Holocaust, said in an interview that UMN leadership “determined that I’m the wrong kind of Israeli and the wrong kind of Jew”. He is now a tenured professor at Stockton University in New Jersey, where he directs a master’s program in Holocaust and genocide studies.

While he was early to argue that Israel’s actions in Gaza amounted to genocide, that position has since been endorsed by scores of scholars, human rights groups, governments and United Nations officials.

“I really wish I had been wrong,” Segal said. “But unfortunately I wasn’t.”

Two days after the University of Minnesota offered Segal the job on 5 June 2024, Karen Painter and Bruno Chaouat, UMN professors and members of the advisory board for the center Segal was tapped to lead, resigned in protest.

In a letter to university leadership, Chaouat, a professor of French and Jewish studies, and Painter, a musicology and Jewish studies professor, accused Segal of “justifying Hamas atrocities” and “blaming Israel” for the 7 October attacks.

Segal’s article cited statements from Israeli officials, a total siege on Gaza and an aerial campaign that, by 13 October 2023, had already dropped 6,000 bombs on the territory. The same piece calls Hamas’s attacks “mass murder” and “a war crime under international law”, characterizations he has made elsewhere, including in the Guardian. “I would never justify Hamas,” he said.

Chaouat did not respond to a request for comment. Painter said that while she had “grave concerns” about Israel’s conduct in Gaza, “Segal was not an appropriate choice to head our Holocaust Center”, and that the search process to fill the position “circumvented the process contemplated at the time the Center was founded, which required consultation with the broader Jewish community”.

As news of the hiring got out, the university began to field media requests. It initially stood by Segal, emails show, with communications staff workshopping public statements and debating whether to say he had received the search committee’s enthusiastic “recommendation” or “support”.

But as pressure intensified, the university began to retreat. On 8 June 2024, a senior member of the communications team warned colleagues that “defending the candidate too much at the moment can be risky”. The team scrapped a sentence from a response it had drafted for media outlets saying that the university did not apply “political litmus tests in hiring”. They also reached out to Segal asking to confirm whether he was “an Israeli native” in order to deal with allegations he was “anti-Israeli”.

Segal responded that he was born in Israel, grew up there and that his parents and sister lived there, as well as friends and colleagues. “I care deeply about the place,” he wrote.

Two days later, UMN leadership informed Segal in a two-sentence email they had changed their minds after “additional members of the University community have come forward to express their interest in providing perspective on the hiring of the positon [sic],” the university’s then interim president, Jeff Ettinger, wrote to Segal.

“Because of the community-facing and leadership role that the Director holds, it is important that these voices are heard,” Ettinger added. “Accordingly, the offer letter of June 5, 2024, is hereby withdrawn to allow an opportunity to determine next steps.” Ettinger offered no further explanation.

The letter came after a barrage of complaints to the university. One donor, Lynne Redleaf, warned that if the university went through with the hire, “it will almost certainly make fundraising for this Center grind to a halt”. She added that she had taken time to “dig in to learn about Raz Segal” and that his references in various writings on Israel to “apartheid” and “settler colonial rule” led her to conclude that Segal was “far too extreme to serve as Director of the Center for Holocaust and Genocide Studies and he is, in fact, an anti-Zionist”.

“His appointment as director is just as offensive as appointing Byron Donalds, who recently praised Jim Crow laws, to lead the African American Studies Department,” Redlead added, referring to a Black, Republican legislator from Florida whose comments about racial segregation had sparked a widespread controversy around that time.

“Thank you for your heads up on this,” Ettinger responded to Redleaf. “Timely and helpful.”

Ettinger did not respond to a request for comment. Redleaf declined to comment.

University leaders also received hundreds of nearly identical emails expressing “concern” with Segal’s appointment and calling his Jewish Currents op-ed “particularly troubling to those who support Israel’s right to defend itself”. Most of those emails included the hashtag #Mothersagainstcollegeantisemitism – referring to a large network of pro-Israel parents who have spearheaded campaigns targeting universities over alleged antisemitism on campuses.

Another email, from the director of the university’s Center for Jewish Studies, warned a university official that the Jewish Community Relations Council (JCRC) of Minnesota and the Dakotas, a group that claims to represent “the public affairs voice of the Jewish community”, was planning to coordinate a “volley” of donor objections, even after the offer had been withdrawn. The director, Natan Paradise, said he had warned the JCRC that the group risked creating an atmosphere so toxic it would be impossible to recruit candidates for the role.

Local legislators entered the fray as well. On 13 June 2024, Marion Rarick, a Republican state representative and lead of the legislature’s higher education committee, wrote in a letter signed by 69 of her colleagues that they were “elated” the university had paused Segal’s hiring but expressed concern it took the “outcry from the Jewish community to bring about this action”.

Segal took issue with the implication that his detractors speak for a broader Jewish community, noting that many Jewish people inside and outside UMN had written to the university to support him. Beth Gendler, director of Jewish Community Action, a progressive group, wrote in an email to Ettinger: “If, as you have indicated, you intend to consult with community members, we implore you not accept the false assertion of one consensus voice for Minnesota Jews.”

Ethan Roberts, the JCRC’s deputy executive director, confirmed that the group organized opposition to Segal’s appointment.

“The issue was not whether Professor Segal had the academic freedom to express controversial opinions. He unquestionably did,” he added. “The question was whether someone holding these views was appropriate to lead a Holocaust and genocide center with a longstanding, community-facing relationship with Holocaust survivors, their descendants, Jewish students, Minnesota’s broader Jewish community, and [sic] had been a longstanding partner to our organization.”

He said that the “minority of Jewish Minnesotans” who supported Segal “had every right to express that position, just as the majority of Jewish Minnesotans who opposed his appointment had every right to express theirs”.

Scores of Jewish professors and community members wrote to the university in defense of Segal, the emails show, including 40 leading Holocaust and genocide scholars who signed a letter arguing that the university’s actions set a “dangerous precedent”.

Ettinger’s move also drew the ire of UMN faculty, who passed a no-confidence vote against him and the university provost; and the American Association of University Professors, which called on the university to reinstate the offer. Dozens more emails flooded in – this time expressing shock and anger over the university’s decision.

“I was dismayed to see this news,” one student affiliated with the Holocaust center wrote. “This makes us worried not only for Raz’s appointment, but for the future of academic freedom and independence in the [University of Minnesota].”

The emails also showed that the university implied to Segal on at least two other occasions it would offer him tenured positions elsewhere in the university.

But more than a year later, no new offer has materialized. Segal said he feared the “stigma” surrounding his withdrawn offer from UMN had damaged his chances to pursue similar academic roles, at least in the US. But he has continued to write about Israel’s actions in Gaza from a scholarly perspective, arguing that genocide in Gaza is “far from over”.

Segal said he had hoped the university would restore the original job offer it had made rather than agree to pay a settlement, but that it was made clear to him that that was “off the table”.

The position remains unfilled.

sentences.zh: 他现在是新泽西州斯托克顿大学的终身教授，指导大屠杀和种族灭绝研究的硕士课程。

blocks.html_en: While he was early to argue that Israel’s actions in Gaza amounted to genocide, that position has since been endorsed by scores of scholars, human rights groups, governments and United Nations officials.

sentences.en: While he was early to argue that Israel’s actions in Gaza amounted to genocide, that position has since been endorsed by scores of scholars, human rights groups, governments and United Nations officials.
sentences.zh: 虽然他很早就认为以色列在加沙的行动相当于种族灭绝，但这一立场此后得到了许多学者、人权组织、政府和联合国官员的认可。

blocks.html_en: “I really wish I had been wrong,” Segal said. “But unfortunately I wasn’t.”

sentences.en: “I really wish I had been wrong,” Segal said.

sentences.en: “But unfortunately I wasn’t.”
sentences.zh: “但不幸的是我不是。”

blocks.html_en: Two days after the University of Minnesota offered Segal the job on 5 June 2024, Karen Painter and Bruno Chaouat, UMN professors and members of the advisory board for the center Segal was tapped to lead, resigned in protest.

sentences.en: Two days after the University of Minnesota offered Segal the job on 5 June 2024, Karen Painter and Bruno Chaouat, UMN professors and members of the advisory board for the center Segal was tapped to lead, resigned in protest.
sentences.zh: 2024 年 6 月 5 日，明尼苏达大学向西格尔提供这份工作两天后，明尼苏达大学教授、该中心顾问委员会成员凯伦·佩因特 (Karen Painter) 和布鲁诺·肖瓦特 (Bruno Chaouat) 被任命为西格尔领导者，但他们辞职以示抗议。

blocks.html_en: In a letter to university leadership, Chaouat, a professor of French and Jewish studies, and Painter, a musicology and Jewish studies professor, accused Segal of “justifying Hamas atrocities” and “blaming Israel” for the 7 October attacks.

sentences.en: In a letter to university leadership, Chaouat, a professor of French and Jewish studies, and Painter, a musicology and Jewish studies professor, accused Segal of “justifying Hamas atrocities” and “blaming Israel” for the 7 October attacks.
sentences.zh: 在给大学领导层的一封信中，法国和犹太研究教授沙瓦特以及音乐学和犹太研究教授佩因特指责西格尔“为哈马斯的暴行辩护”并“指责以色列”对 10 月 7 日的袭击负责。

blocks.html_en: Segal’s article cited statements from Israeli officials, a total siege on Gaza and an aerial campaign that, by 13 October 2023, had already dropped 6,000 bombs on the territory. The same piece calls Hamas’s attacks “mass murder” and “a war crime under international law”, characterizations he has made elsewhere, including in the Guardian. “I would never justify Hamas,” he said.

sentences.en: Segal’s article cited statements from Israeli officials, a total siege on Gaza and an aerial campaign that, by 13 October 2023, had already dropped 6,000 bombs on the territory.
sentences.zh: 西格尔的文章引用了以色列官员的声明，称其对加沙进行了全面围困，并进行了空袭，截至 2023 年 10 月 13 日，已在该地区投下 6,000 枚炸弹。

sentences.en: The same piece calls Hamas’s attacks “mass murder” and “a war crime under international law”, characterizations he has made elsewhere, including in the Guardian.

sentences.en: “I would never justify Hamas,” he said.
sentences.zh: “我永远不会为哈马斯辩护，”他说。

Painter said that while she had “grave concerns” about Israel’s conduct in Gaza, “Segal was not an appropriate choice to head our Holocaust Center”, and that the search process to fill the position “circumvented the process contemplated at the time the Center was founded, which required consultation with the broader Jewish community”.

sentences.en: Chaouat did not respond to a request for comment.
sentences.zh: Chaouat 没有回应置评请求。

sentences.zh: 佩因特表示，虽然她对以色列在加沙的行为感到“严重关切”，但“西格尔并不是领导我们大屠杀中心的合适人选”，而且填补这一职位的搜寻过程“绕过了该中心成立时所设想的程序，该程序需要与更广泛的犹太社区进行协商”。

blocks.html_en: As news of the hiring got out, the university began to field media requests. It initially stood by Segal, emails show, with communications staff workshopping public statements and debating whether to say he had received the search committee’s enthusiastic “recommendation” or “support”.

blocks.html_en: But as pressure intensified, the university began to retreat. On 8 June 2024, a senior member of the communications team warned colleagues that “defending the candidate too much at the moment can be risky”. The team scrapped a sentence from a response it had drafted for media outlets saying that the university did not apply “political litmus tests in hiring”. They also reached out to Segal asking to confirm whether he was “an Israeli native” in order to deal with allegations he was “anti-Israeli”.

sentences.en: But as pressure intensified, the university began to retreat.
sentences.zh: 但随着压力的加大，大学开始退缩。

sentences.zh: 他们还联系了西格尔，要求确认他是否是“以色列人”，以应对他“反以色列”的指控。

blocks.html_en: Segal responded that he was born in Israel, grew up there and that his parents and sister lived there, as well as friends and colleagues. “I care deeply about the place,” he wrote.

sentences.zh: 西格尔回答说，他出生在以色列，在那里长大，他的父母和妹妹以及朋友和同事都住在那里。

sentences.en: “I care deeply about the place,” he wrote.
sentences.zh: “我非常关心这个地方，”他写道。

sentences.en: Two days later, UMN leadership informed Segal in a two-sentence email they had changed their minds after “additional members of the University community have come forward to express their interest in providing perspective on the hiring of the positon [sic],” the university’s then interim president, Jeff Ettinger, wrote to Segal.
sentences.zh: 两天后，UMN 领导层在一封两句话的电子邮件中通知西格尔，在“大学社区的其他成员站出来表达了他们对招聘该职位的看法的兴趣[原文如此]”后，该大学当时的临时校长杰夫·埃丁格 (Jeff Ettinger) 写信给西格尔，他们改变了主意。

sentences.en: Demonstrators studied and visited after setting up tents on the lawn of the University of Minnesota campus in Minneapolis on 29 April 2024.

blocks.html_en: The letter came after a barrage of complaints to the university. One donor, Lynne Redleaf, warned that if the university went through with the hire, “it will almost certainly make fundraising for this Center grind to a halt”. She added that she had taken time to “dig in to learn about Raz Segal” and that his references in various writings on Israel to “apartheid” and “settler colonial rule” led her to conclude that Segal was “far too extreme to serve as Director of the Center for Holocaust and Genocide Studies and he is, in fact, an anti-Zionist”.

sentences.en: The letter came after a barrage of complaints to the university.

sentences.en: She added that she had taken time to “dig in to learn about Raz Segal” and that his references in various writings on Israel to “apartheid” and “settler colonial rule” led her to conclude that Segal was “far too extreme to serve as Director of the Center for Holocaust and Genocide Studies and he is, in fact, an anti-Zionist”.
sentences.zh: 她补充说，她花了一些时间“深入了解拉兹·西格尔”，他在有关以色列的各种著作中提到“种族隔离”和“定居者殖民统治”，这让她得出结论，西格尔“过于极端，不适合担任大屠杀和种族灭绝研究中心主任，事实上，他是一个反犹太复国主义者”。

blocks.html_en: “His appointment as director is just as offensive as appointing Byron Donalds, who recently praised Jim Crow laws, to lead the African American Studies Department,” Redlead added, referring to a Black, Republican legislator from Florida whose comments about racial segregation had sparked a widespread controversy around that time.

sentences.en: “His appointment as director is just as offensive as appointing Byron Donalds, who recently praised Jim Crow laws, to lead the African American Studies Department,” Redlead added, referring to a Black, Republican legislator from Florida whose comments about racial segregation had sparked a widespread controversy around that time.
sentences.zh: 雷德利德补充道：“任命他为主任，与任命拜伦·唐纳德（拜伦·唐纳德最近赞扬种族隔离法）领导非裔美国人研究部一样令人反感。”他指的是一位来自佛罗里达州的黑人共和党议员，他有关种族隔离的言论当时引发了广泛争议。

blocks.html_en: “Thank you for your heads up on this,” Ettinger responded to Redleaf. “Timely and helpful.”

sentences.zh: “及时且乐于助人。”

sentences.en: University leaders also received hundreds of nearly identical emails expressing “concern” with Segal’s appointment and calling his Jewish Currents op-ed “particularly troubling to those who support Israel’s right to defend itself”.
sentences.zh: 大学领导还收到了数百封几乎相同的电子邮件，表达了对西格尔任命的“担忧”，并称他的《犹太潮流》专栏文章“对那些支持以色列自卫权的人来说尤其令人不安”。

sentences.en: Most of those emails included the hashtag #Mothersagainstcollegeantisemitism – referring to a large network of pro-Israel parents who have spearheaded campaigns targeting universities over alleged antisemitism on campuses.

blocks.html_en: Another email, from the director of the university’s Center for Jewish Studies, warned a university official that the Jewish Community Relations Council (JCRC) of Minnesota and the Dakotas, a group that claims to represent “the public affairs voice of the Jewish community”, was planning to coordinate a “volley” of donor objections, even after the offer had been withdrawn. The director, Natan Paradise, said he had warned the JCRC that the group risked creating an atmosphere so toxic it would be impossible to recruit candidates for the role.

sentences.zh: 另一封来自该大学犹太研究中心主任的电子邮件警告一名大学官员，明尼苏达州和达科他州的犹太社区关系委员会（JCRC）声称代表“犹太社区公共事务的声音”，该组织正计划协调一系列捐助者的反对意见，即使在提议被撤回之后也是如此。

blocks.html_en: Local legislators entered the fray as well. On 13 June 2024, Marion Rarick, a Republican state representative and lead of the legislature’s higher education committee, wrote in a letter signed by 69 of her colleagues that they were “elated” the university had paused Segal’s hiring but expressed concern it took the “outcry from the Jewish community to bring about this action”.

sentences.en: Local legislators entered the fray as well.

content_html_zh:
明尼苏达大学 (UMN) 于 2024 年 6 月向历史学家拉兹·西格尔 (Raz Segal) 发出邀请，担任其大屠杀和种族灭绝研究中心的负责人，这是在学术委员会经过严格的搜索过程后几乎一致推荐的情况下做出的。 学者们热情赞扬了西格尔，一位委员会成员形容他的演讲“令人惊叹”。

但在提出邀请五天后，该大学突然撤回了该邀请，理由是它从社区成员那里收到了“观点”。 这一逆转是在西格尔对以色列在加沙行动的批评引起强烈反对后发生的，他在《犹太潮流》2023 年 10 月发表的一篇专栏文章中称这是“教科书般的种族灭绝案例”。 西格尔的批评者谴责了这篇在 10 月 7 日以色列袭击事件发生几天后发表的文章，指责他为哈马斯的罪行辩护 — — 西格尔否认了这一说法，而且这篇文章也没有支持。

上周，在该提议被撤销两年多后，西格尔与大学达成了 25 万美元的和解协议。 按照此类和解的标准，交易条款规定，支付款项并不意味着 UMN 承认存在不当行为。 该大学没有回应置评请求。

西格尔表示，这笔巨款应该会鼓励数十名因批评以色列而受到解雇、停职和调查等惩罚的学者进行“反击”。

西格尔通过公共记录请求获得了数十封电子邮件，揭露了捐助者、立法者和亲以色列活动人士对大学官员的压力运动，之后达成了和解。 这些文件独家分享给《卫报》，揭示了大学如何从捍卫西格尔到最终收回聘用他的决定。

“我们不能允许像拉兹·西格尔这样公然反犹太复国主义者的人领导大屠杀研究系[原文如此]，”一位捐助者写信给该大学董事会主席。 “如果这个问题得不到解决，很多人都会放弃对大学的承诺。” 据西格尔称，数百封电子邮件按照相同的模板发送到该大学，表明这是一场协调一致的活动。

代表他的宪法权利中心认为，公立大学针对西格尔的行为是违宪的，因为他们对他受宪法保护的言论进行报复。

“西格尔博士有勇气拉响警报，试图阻止以色列对巴勒斯坦人的种族灭绝，”该中心法律副主任玛丽亚·拉胡德说。 “为此，明尼苏达大学管理部门推翻了教职员工的意愿，撤销了他的工作机会，这违反了第一修正案和学术自由的基本原则。”

西格尔是犹太人，拥有以色列和美国双重公民身份，是四名大屠杀幸存者的孙子，也是一位研究犹太世界和大屠杀的学者。他在接受采访时表示，UMN 领导层“认定我是错误的以色列人和错误的犹太人”。 他现在是新泽西州斯托克顿大学的终身教授，指导大屠杀和种族灭绝研究的硕士课程。

虽然他很早就认为以色列在加沙的行动相当于种族灭绝，但这一立场此后得到了许多学者、人权组织、政府和联合国官员的认可。

“我真希望我是错的，”西格尔说。 “但不幸的是我不是。”

2024 年 6 月 5 日，明尼苏达大学向西格尔提供这份工作两天后，明尼苏达大学教授、该中心顾问委员会成员凯伦·佩因特 (Karen Painter) 和布鲁诺·肖瓦特 (Bruno Chaouat) 被任命为西格尔领导者，但他们辞职以示抗议。

在给大学领导层的一封信中，法国和犹太研究教授沙瓦特以及音乐学和犹太研究教授佩因特指责西格尔“为哈马斯的暴行辩护”并“指责以色列”对 10 月 7 日的袭击负责。

西格尔的文章引用了以色列官员的声明，称其对加沙进行了全面围困，并进行了空袭，截至 2023 年 10 月 13 日，已在该地区投下 6,000 枚炸弹。 同一篇文章称哈马斯的袭击是“大规模谋杀”和“国际法规定的战争罪”，他在其他地方（包括《卫报》）也曾对此进行过描述。 “我永远不会为哈马斯辩护，”他说。

Chaouat 没有回应置评请求。 佩因特表示，虽然她对以色列在加沙的行为感到“严重关切”，但“西格尔并不是领导我们大屠杀中心的合适人选”，而且填补这一职位的搜寻过程“绕过了该中心成立时所设想的程序，该程序需要与更广泛的犹太社区进行协商”。

随着招聘消息传出，该大学开始回应媒体请求。 电子邮件显示，它最初支持西格尔，通讯人员讨论公开声明，并讨论是否说他收到了选拔委员会的热情“推荐”或“支持”。

但随着压力的加大，大学开始退缩。 2024 年 6 月 8 日，传播团队的一名高级成员警告同事，“目前过多地为候选人辩护可能会有风险”。 该团队取消了为媒体起草的一份回应中的一句话，称该大学没有在招聘中应用“政治试金石”。 他们还联系了西格尔，要求确认他是否是“以色列人”，以应对他“反以色列”的指控。

西格尔回答说，他出生在以色列，在那里长大，他的父母和妹妹以及朋友和同事都住在那里。 “我非常关心这个地方，”他写道。

两天后，UMN 领导层在一封两句话的电子邮件中通知西格尔，在“大学社区的其他成员站出来表达了他们对招聘该职位的看法的兴趣[原文如此]”后，该大学当时的临时校长杰夫·埃丁格 (Jeff Ettinger) 写信给西格尔，他们改变了主意。

“由于主任承担着面向社区和领导的角色，因此听取这些声音非常重要，”埃廷格补充道。 “因此，特此撤回 2024 年 6 月 5 日的录取通知书，以便有机会确定后续步骤。” 埃廷格没有提供进一步的解释。

这封信是在向大学提出一系列投诉后发出的。 一位捐赠者林恩·雷德利夫 (Lynne Redleaf) 警告说，如果该大学接受了聘用，“几乎肯定会使该中心的筹款活动陷入停滞”。 她补充说，她花了一些时间“深入了解拉兹·西格尔”，他在有关以色列的各种著作中提到“种族隔离”和“定居者殖民统治”，这让她得出结论，西格尔“过于极端，不适合担任大屠杀和种族灭绝研究中心主任，事实上，他是一个反犹太复国主义者”。

雷德利德补充道：“任命他为主任，与任命拜伦·唐纳德（拜伦·唐纳德最近赞扬种族隔离法）领导非裔美国人研究部一样令人反感。”他指的是一位来自佛罗里达州的黑人共和党议员，他有关种族隔离的言论当时引发了广泛争议。

“感谢您对此的提醒，”埃廷格对雷德利夫回应道。 “及时且乐于助人。”

埃廷格没有回应置评请求。 雷德利夫拒绝置评。

大学领导还收到了数百封几乎相同的电子邮件，表达了对西格尔任命的“担忧”，并称他的《犹太潮流》专栏文章“对那些支持以色列自卫权的人来说尤其令人不安”。 这些电子邮件中的大多数都包含主题标签#Mothersagainstcollegeantisemitism——指的是一个由亲以色列家长组成的大型网络，他们带头针对大学发起针对校园所谓反犹太主义的运动。

另一封来自该大学犹太研究中心主任的电子邮件警告一名大学官员，明尼苏达州和达科他州的犹太社区关系委员会（JCRC）声称代表“犹太社区公共事务的声音”，该组织正计划协调一系列捐助者的反对意见，即使在提议被撤回之后也是如此。 主管纳坦·帕拉代斯 (Natan Paradise) 表示，他已警告 JCRC，该组织可能会营造一种有毒的氛围，以至于不可能招募到该职位的候选人。

当地立法者也加入了争论。 2024 年 6 月 13 日，共和党州众议员兼立法机关高等教育委员会负责人马里昂·拉里克 (Marion Rarick) 在一封由 69 名同事签名的信中写道，他们对大学暂停西格尔的招聘感到“高兴”，但表示担心“在犹太社区的强烈抗议下才采取这一行动”。

西格尔对他的批评者代表更广泛的犹太社区的暗示提出了异议，并指出UMN内外的许多犹太人都写信给该大学支持他。 进步团体“犹太社区行动”的主任贝丝·詹德勒在给艾廷格的一封电子邮件中写道：“如果正如您所指出的，您打算与社区成员协商，我们恳请您不要接受明尼苏达犹太人的一个共识声音的错误主张。”

JCRC 副执行主任伊森·罗伯茨 (Ethan Roberts) 证实，该组织组织了反对西格尔任命的活动。

“问题不在于西格尔教授是否有学术自由来表达有争议的观点。 毫无疑问他做到了，”他补充道。 “问题是，持有这些观点的人是否适合领导一个与大屠杀幸存者、他们的后代、犹太学生、明尼苏达州更广泛的犹太社区建立长期、面向社区的关系的大屠杀和种族灭绝中心，并且[原文如此]一直是我们组织的长期合作伙伴。”

他说，支持西格尔的“少数犹太明尼苏达人”“完全有权表达这一立场，就像反对他任命的大多数犹太明尼苏达人完全有权表达他们的立场一样”。

电子邮件显示，数十名犹太教授和社区成员写信给该大学为西格尔辩护，其中包括 40 名大屠杀和种族灭绝领域的知名学者，他们签署了一封信，认为该大学的行为开创了“危险的先例”。

埃廷格的举动也引起了UMN教员的愤怒，他们通过了对他和大学教务长的不信任投票。美国大学教授协会呼吁大学恢复这一提议。 又有数十封电子邮件涌入，这一次表达了对大学决定的震惊和愤怒。

“看到这个消息我很沮丧，”大屠杀中心的一名学生写道。 “这不仅让我们对拉兹的任命感到担忧，而且对[明尼苏达大学]学术自由和独立的未来感到担忧。”

这些电子邮件还显示，该大学至少在另外两次场合向西格尔暗示，将向他提供大学其他地方的终身职位。

但一年多过去了，新的报价还没有落实。 西格尔表示，他担心他从UMN撤回录取通知书所带来的“耻辱”会损害他寻求类似学术职位的机会，至少在美国是这样。 但他继续从学术角度撰写以色列在加沙的行动，认为加沙的种族灭绝“远未结束”。

西格尔表示，他原本希望学校恢复原来的工作邀请，而不是同意支付和解金，但他已经明确表示，这是“不可能的”。

该职位仍空缺。
